PROJECT=MOARTN SURVEY="Reelfoot_Rift" YEAR=2017 PROCESSEDBY=PAB PROCESSINGSOFTWARE=mtmerge/mtft/mtedit
TRANSFER FUNCTIONS HAVE BEEN ROTATED INTO GEOGRAPHIC COORDINATES. Processing steps: Time-series: electric and magnetic field data were collected in a geomagnetic north and east coordinate system using wideband magnetotelluric instrumentation (Zen receivers from Zonge International) at each site location. Individual magnetic and electric channel files were merged using program Mtmerge64.exe from Zonge International. Resulting merged binary files have been converted to ASCII format (*.asc files). Fourier spectra were calculated from windowed time-series data and used to calculate cross- and auto-power spectra via program Mtft24x64.exe from Zonge International. Remote reference processing, in which synchronously recording stations are processed together to remove incoherent noise, was carried out using all possible station combinations. Impedance and tipper transfer functions were calculated at each station using program MTedit64.exe from Zonge International. System and sensor responses (antenna.cal file) were accounted for during this process and transfer function estimates were made for particular frequency bandwidths for each data run (4096 and 256 Hz sampling frequencies). Transfer function estimates were constructed by selecting optimal TF estimates at each period from a series of processing runs using different reference combinations. High (4096 Hz sampling rate) and low (256 Hz sampling rate) frequency wideband recordings provided TF estimates for 1000-1 Hz and 0.001-1 Hz, respectively. So-called optimal TFs were selected based on examination of phase slope, smooth curve assumptions, and operator discretion. TF estimates provided in the *.edi files and displayed in the *.png files have been rotated to geographic coordinates (X = North).
